original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Actual arbitrary-dirty-role circuit optimum of the mixed S4 tuple diag([2143],[3142],[4231],[2143],1,...) at prices (2,1,2) in the formal F2[S4] register model of PR2583/PR2998: is a cost-20 word possible (coordinate-cut bound 20, direct words 21)? Decided here for r=4 and r=5 roles by a window-pruned exhaustive search; r>=6 not searched.
scope_change_reason: The drawn card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the three-register obstruction. Its live successor in Discussion2570 is the explicit open question of PR2998: coordinate cuts stop at 20 while direct words cost 21 for this mixed tuple, so whether cut pricing is exact for mixed nonabelian tuples needs a circuit-level decision. This package answers it for four and five roles with a window (prefix-tightness) lemma used as a pruning device instead of another cut class.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit track (formal register model only). The static coordinate-cut LP (per-letter charges, value 20) is not attained for this mixed nonabelian tuple on at most five roles (optimum 21): the tuple has no joint saving over separate words at width <= 5, so cut-LP tariffs cannot be assumed to price shared mixed-target words, and any cross-role saving would need two or more dirty spectators (r>=6) or another model change. It does not change the bit supplier, the binding complex primitive, the selected moment or kappa.
stop_rule: Hard stop for searching at the iteration experiment deadline 2026-10-19T00:59:18Z; roles r in {4,5} only, total cost 20 only (costs below 20 are already excluded by PR2583's L = inv+c1+c3 bound, whose value 20 is PR2998's cut value), prices (2,1,2) only, no new cut classes, no r>=6.
evidence: PROOF.md: inherited normal form (Ross Richardson PR1989, reused in PR2583: free maps absorbed, trailing scalar forced to I by augmentation), inherited cut-rank potentials (two blocks each), new window lemma and prefix-tightness corollary used as a pruning device, inherited count consequence made explicit (PR2583's L = inv+c1+c3 bound; PR2998's twelve-paid / eight-exterior observation): cost 20 forces label counts (4,4,4). Exhaustive target-end DFS over all 360 (r=4) and 1488 (r=5, 7 orbit representatives of the first peeled letter) gates per step: no prefix survives depth 8, zero words; with the explicit cost-21 direct word (checked exactly), the four- and five-role optima are exactly 21. RESULT.json records node counts. Cross-checks: separately written explicit-matrix C++ engine (full r=4 tree and the r=5 representative tree, node-for-node); Python explicit-matrix search (both r=3 sub-tuple trees, first three r=4 depths, r=5 depth 1); unpruned frozenset group-algebra brute-force count 146 = pruned primary count = exactly rechecked independent survivors on a 2-role instance where 104 of the 146 words use a mixing gate; r=4 positive control (4312 variant: a direct word is found); scalar negative control (4231 at counts (1,3,1)). Exact rational coordinate-cut LPs over all 2^24 regular cuts give 3-target sub-tuple LP values 15 and 16 against optima 16 and 17 (direct r=3 searches and transfer). Only verify.py --full replays the complete r=4/r=5 trees and the LPs.

open_questions.question: Does a sixth (second spectator) or further dirty role allow a cost-20 word for diag([2143],[3142],[4231],[2143],1,1,...) at (2,1,2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package decides r=4 and r=5 (optimum 21 in both). Coordinate cuts allow 20 for every r, so only workspace can still realize the cut value; a positive answer would be the first known restored-spectator saving in this weighted model.
open_questions.first_step: Widen search.cpp's block rows to 64 bits first (the inv block has 6r = 36 columns at r=6; the engine refuses r > 5), then run it at r=6 (6048 gates per step) with the first-peeled-letter symmetry, possibly enlarged by GL_2(F2) on the two spectator roles. For scale only: about 33K nodes per surviving first letter at r=4 and about 34K per representative at r=5; the r=6 cost is unknown (four times as many gates per step, wider blocks, possibly a larger tree), so any runtime estimate is a rough guess. Budget and post the five-point expansion decision in Discussion2570 first.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this card stop rule (r<=5); needs a separately budgeted run.

open_questions.question: Is there a uniform (all-r) invariant explaining why the window-feasible prefix tree dies at depth 8, i.e. a written stronger-than-cut obstruction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A uniform argument would turn the finite r<=5 exclusion into the arbitrary-workspace 21 theorem that PR2998 left open, and would give a reusable tool for mixed nonabelian tariffs beyond cut LPs.
open_questions.first_step: Inspect the 381816 depth-7 survivors at r=4 (or the 52422 at r=5) and identify which window (inv, c1 or c3, which block) kills every depth-8 extension; try to express it as a chronological (precedence) rank inequality valid for all r.
open_questions.blocked_by: None technically; needs a separate session.
